source.title: Uniform convergence may be unable to explain generalization in deep learning

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and measures test error, a different setup from the fixed-epoch large-batch claim in V5. Its main experiments evaluate generalization bounds, not the versions’ interventions or measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test error changing with training-set size, depth, and batch size. Only the batch-size test-error sweep bears on a mapped version; results about bounds, norms, and training-set-size scaling do not establish the versions’ specified claims. Figure-only error values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study tests explanations of generalization through uniform-convergence bounds. Its batch-size sweep reports test error under a margin-based stopping rule, so it does not test V5's fixed-epoch comparison. No other named version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: existing bounds can worsen with sample size, and the constructed settings show failure of two-sided uniform convergence even after accounting for implicit bias. The authors advocate exploring other approaches; they do not prove that every possible generalization bound must fail.
record.recipe_differences: The study empirically evaluates generalization bounds and constructs theoretical examples; its batch-size experiment uses a margin-based stopping rule rather than the fixed-epoch recipe in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: In the MNIST experiment, test error increases slightly as batch size increases. The reported bound behavior also varies with batch size, depth, width, and training-set size, but those are not claim-version outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST with m=16384, test error increases slightly with batch size when training stops after 99% of training examples achieve margin 10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger batches can have slightly worse test error under a common margin-based stopping criterion.

fits_no_version.finding: Interpolating between weights learned from two independent dataset draws preserves test error; the explored parameter space grows with training-set size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Solutions from a shared initialization can lie in a connected region of similar test error despite increasing parameter-space distances.

fits_no_version.finding: Existing bounds can increase with training-set size, and constructed settings yield nearly vacuous two-sided uniform-convergence guarantees despite small generalization error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uniform convergence can fail to explain generalization even after restricting the hypothesis class to outputs of the learning algorithm.

record.problems: Batch-size test-error results are presented in a figure without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The batch sweep uses a margin-based stopping criterion rather than a fixed epoch budget. The theoretical ReLU example is a constructed adversarial-spheres task, not natural image labels.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. The paper’s test-error trends with training-set size, width, and depth do not measure a named version’s specified outcome. Generalization-bound values and weight-norm trends are not rows for the mapped versions.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training and held-out performance.
Test-error changes when widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers under specified tuning budgets.
Large versus small batches at fixed epoch budgets, workload-dependent thresholds, and recipe adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, dropout strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: A different stopping rule is an untested condition of V5, not evidence that V5 needs qualifying. The slight batch-size trend therefore warrants no limits_scope verdict. The flat-minima discussion does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: The paper cites memorization of random labels and good natural-label generalization as motivation but does not test both on the same models or recipes.
It does not measure test error while widening networks beyond the width needed for zero training error.

The paper varies batch size and reports test error changes, but does not hold epoch count fixed or identify a workload-dependent batch threshold. Batch-specific plotted test-error values are figure-only and are retained as rows below.
The paper does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
No memorized-example removal experiment is reported.
